decisions.notes: A fourth source already in the packet (herald-dispatch.com) states the ordinance was 'approved unanimously without discussion... during a special meeting July 9' -- this conflicts with the row's July 21 date. I searched further and found (a) the Daily Independent's own preview article explicitly scheduling the second/final reading for the regular July 21 meeting, (b) a Daily Independent legal public notice indexed in search results (text snippet: 'On July 21, 2026, the Boyd County Fiscal Court passed Ordinance 2026-03, imposing a six (6) month moratorium...' -- matching the row's existing legal_basis, 'Ordinance 2026-03') that I could not archive after repeated attempts (page returned ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED each time, so it is not cited as formal evidence), and (c) confirmation that a special meeting was indeed called for July 9, which fits a first-reading-at-a-special-meeting theory better than a final-adoption-at-a-special-meeting theory given the Daily Independent's own contemporaneous reporting. On balance the weight of evidence supports keeping the row's July 21, 2026 date; the Herald-Dispatch's July 9 claim looks like a reporting error, not a genuine second date. Confidence held at 0.85 rather than higher given the unresolved conflict in reporting.
